title: Fourier restriction as curvature vs energy focus
summary: Restriction asks how much a Fourier transform of a measure supported on a curved hypersurface (sphere) can concentrate. Flat directions allow coherent focusing along lines; curvature forces cancellation. Knapp example: small spherical cap ≈ flat ⇒ energy lives in a thin tube.
math: In R^3, the conjectured critical restriction exponent is often packaged as p=3 in popular accounts; best published range historically far from critical.

title: Wave packets = tubes; Restriction ⇒ Kakeya
summary: Partition sphere into caps → each packet lives in a long thin tube with radius ~ sqrt(length) scaling relative to cap size; all directions appear. Tube-overlap control is needed for restriction, so Kakeya-type geometry is necessary (not sufficient).

title: Progress ledger toward p=3
summary: Stein–Tomas 1975: p≥4. Then Bourgain, Tao, Bourgain–Guth, Guth polynomial partitioning, broom structures, Wang collaborators: progressive improvements; late-2024 popular account cites 22/7≈3.143 with remaining gap ≈0.143 to the believed critical 3. Exponents across papers are not always identical formulations—compare carefully.

title: Two-ends geometric reduction (Wang–Wu ~2024)
summary: Instead of pure analytic inequalities, reduce restriction to a geometric intersection hypothesis for tube families with a two-ends mass condition (mass cannot pile only at one end). If two-ends holds in 3D, restriction would follow. Plane analogues partly settled; 3D open. Links to Furstenberg technology.

title: Post-Fields open race
summary: After Kakeya foundation (2025) and Wang Fields 2026, the video frames restriction + related towers as the next decade's prize landscape—not a prediction of winners.
